nodes.reason: The one-line Lean proposition matches every prose hypothesis and the integrability-on-L conclusion. Compact containment gives the smooth cutoff; multiplying it by the arbitrary constant covector produces an admissible test form. Linearity and the assumed test-form integrability yield an integrable function agreeing with v(·)(c) on measurable L. The empty case is covered. No measurability or local-finiteness assumption on the original data is silently added, and no parent or sibling theorem is used.

The exact type correctly expresses smoothness of every finite order, compact support and support containment. The proof constructs admissible mollifications, verifies their support and common bound, proves pointwise convergence, and applies dominated convergence separately under both measures. The empty-support case is handled. The supplied support-preserving approximation alternative also matches the pinned library. This is a complete independent proof, not deferred proof planning.

The prose and one-line type agree, including integrability, Borel measurability, global boundedness and vanishing outside O. Borel representatives legitimately preserve the integrals. Positive and negative densities define finite measures, and the integration identity has integrable terms. The explicit cutoffs have compact support inside V and increase to its indicator, including the full-space case. Finite-measure π–λ uniqueness gives equality of restrictions, which proves the bounded-integrand conclusion. No circular dependence or missing regularity assumption remains.

The exact type matches the stated coordinate expansion and the pinned definitions of coefficients and wedges. Determinant evaluation establishes the Kronecker property; equal finite ranges force equal increasing indices, justifying the zero-column argument. Sorting and the alternating sign rule extend equality to injective basis tuples, and basis extensionality completes the proof. The k=0 and k>P cases are covered. The proof is independent of the selected parent and other active branches.
